title: The Edge of Knowing
statement: A city records what has been seen; portraits and specimens turn fragments into inference. Beyond their fragile overlap, Earth rises as the portion of the world that remains irreducibly beyond the frame.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent the boundary between what you know, what you infer, and what you cannot know.

actions.title: The Edge of Knowing
actions.statement: A city records what has been seen; portraits and specimens turn fragments into inference. Beyond their fragile overlap, Earth rises as the portion of the world that remains irreducibly beyond the frame.

notes.note: Establish a triptych-like field of certainty: archival city as the known, an oval witness portrait and specimen as inference, and Earthrise as the unknowable horizon. The first pass builds the large compositional anchors and registers the title and statement.

actions.title: The Edge of Knowing
actions.statement: A city records what has been seen; portraits and specimens turn fragments into inference. Beyond their fragile overlap, Earth rises as the portion of the world that remains irreducibly beyond the frame.

notes.note: The initial anchors read clearly against the lunar black. I will add one circular, weathered mirror-disc as a quiet threshold behind the living and archival fragments, making the boundary between observation and projection more explicit without crowding the frame.

The composition is complete: a documentary city, portrait, mirror-disc, botanical plate, and flamingo occupy a shared lunar threshold while the surrounding black field preserves the unknowable. The visual hierarchy and negative space are balanced, and the title and statement are present.
